issue.title: Request: maintained Windows x64 codec-enabled CEF 156 minimal SDK
issue.body:
Could you publish a Windows x64 codec-enabled minimal SDK for the current maintained CEF 156 branch (CEF 156.0.27 / Chromium 156.0.8078.96, or a newer supported security revision)?

Your 154.0.34 Windows SDK successfully decoded H.264/AAC MP4, standalone AAC and VP9 in our disposable native C-ABI host under CrossOver: 28 H.264 frames, 29 VP9 frames, advancing playback time, no media errors, clean shutdown. Native Windows qualification remains separate. We already ship 156, so 154 is unsuitable as an update to existing browser profiles.

Requested artifact:

- Windows x64 minimal distribution with `proprietary_codecs=true ffmpeg_branding=Chrome`.
- Matching headers, import library, sandbox bootstrap, runtime DLLs and Resources, retaining the Chromium sandbox.
- Pinned upstream revisions, build flags and any patches, SHA-256, CEF/Chromium/FFmpeg notices and applicable redistribution terms.
- Your expected security update cadence, without assuming an SLA.

We can test the matching SDK in the isolated C-ABI host before integrating it. This is an availability request, not authorization for paid work or a request for you to certify our application.

Thank you for publishing these builds.

comment.body:
Hopefully, you can keep updating these packages as newer CEF versions become available. I'm using your work in my custom-built browser, Vibify:

https://github.com/spooky8823/Vibify

I really appreciate your work and the effort that goes into maintaining this package. It has been genuinely useful for my project. Thanks for making it available!
